method.value: CASA imaging with Hogbom clean, natural weighting; linear continuum fit to line-free channels

evidence.quote: A first order fit to the line-free channels was used to estimate the continuum emission removal. The Hogbom algorithm was used for the clean.

analysis_steps.goal: Identify methyl formate lines and check blending

method.value: Match to lab rest frequencies; check overlap using Splatalogue; classify B/NB/ND

evidence.quote: Any possible overlap of other lines was examined based on the molecular line database, Splatalogue (cite: rem07).

key_parameters.value: NB if contaminant weaker than ~10% of methyl formate line

evidence.quote: When the intensity of the contaminated line is weaker than about 10% of the methyl formate line, it was considered to be no blend.

analysis_steps.goal: Map distributions and extract line parameters

method.value: Integrated intensity maps 4-12 km/s; Gaussian fits to spectra of Compact Ridge and Hot Core giving T, FWHM, VLSR, W

evidence.quote: The spectra of the Hot Core can be fitted by a single Gaussian and the center of velocity is about 7.3  km s$^{-1}$.

fitting.value: Single Gaussian for Hot Core; two components for Compact Ridge

evidence.quote: there are two velocity components at the Compact Ridge corresponding to $V_{LSR}$ of about 7.3 km s$^{-1}$ and 9.1 km s$^{-1}$

validation.value: Compared with MF1/MF2 of Favre et al. 2011

evidence.quote: In the paper by (cite: fav11), the Compact Ridge corresponds to MF1 and the Hot Core corresponds to MF2.

method.value: Q = Q_rot Q_tor with analytic Q_rot and sum over torsional states up to v_t=2

evidence.quote: The partition function used in this study was $Q=Q_{rot}Q_{tor}$.

assumptions.value: Same torsional energies for A and E sublevels

evidence.quote: for Equation (2), $\Delta E$=132 cm$^{-1}$ (cite: tud12) and $\Delta E$=250 cm$^{-1}$ (cite: sen05) were assumed for $v_{t}=$1 and 2, respectively, for both the A and E sublevels.

validation.value: Compared with JPL direct sum and Favre et al. 2014; within 1% at 9.375 K

evidence.quote: our adopted simple and easy-to-calculate model is within a 1$\%$ error even at 9.375 K.

analysis_steps.goal: Rotation diagrams: temperatures and column densities

method.value: Rotation diagrams per component, per torsional state (T_rot) and all states combined (T_eff = T_vib); LTE; optically thick lines excluded

evidence.quote: We set the criteria to exclude lines with $S\mu^{2} \geq 35$ in $v_{t}$=0 for the 7.3 km s$^{-1}$ component in the Compact Ridge and Hot Core to avoid the optically thick transitions.
Therefore, optically thick transitions and contaminated transitions were removed to determine the rotational temperature and vibrational temperature.

assumptions.value: LTE, optically thin after exclusion; tau~2 at Smu2~35 assuming 150 K

evidence.quote: Assuming a temperature of 150 K, which may be a little higher for the Compact Ridge but reasonable for the Hot Core, optical depths $\tau$ of a few lines were calculated and they were about two.

validation.value: Removal of optically thick lines improved fit; compared with Favre 2011/2014 and Takano 2012

evidence.quote: Removal of the optically thick transitions improved the quality of the fit.
The data were analyzed by using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package.
Any possible overlap of other lines was examined based on the molecular line database, Splatalogue (cite: rem07).

used_for.value: Line assignment and partition function comparison

evidence.quote: the assignment was done based on the JPL catalogue (cite: pik98)

results_numeric.quantity: Effective temperature, Compact Ridge, 7.3 km/s component
Rotational temperature v_t=0, Compact Ridge 7.3 km/s

evidence.quote: Briefly, 84, 68, and 62 transitions were found to be due to the transitions of methyl formate in $v_{t} =$0, 1 and 2, respectively.

findings_qualitative.value: Intensity maps of v_t=0,1,2 have similar distributions with peaks on Compact Ridge and Hot Core

evidence.quote: The intensity maps in the ground, first, and second torsional excited states have quite similar distributions.

claims.hypothesis: Do Compact Ridge and Hot Core show distinct velocity structure in methyl formate?
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits of ALMA SV spectra
claims.result: Compact Ridge has 7.3 and 9.1 km/s components; Hot Core only 7.3

evidence.quote: Toward the Compact Ridge, two different velocity components at 7.3 and 9.1 km s$^{-1}$ were confirmed, while a single component at 7.3 km s$^{-1}$ was identified towards the Hot Core.

claims.hypothesis: Is T_vib higher than T_rot as found with single dish?
claims.result: T_rot and T_vib agree for Hot Core and CR 9.1; T_rot > T_vib for CR 7.3
claims.finding: Single-dish difference not reproduced; likely beam dilution/narrow Eu range

evidence.quote: The rotational temperature and vibrational temperatures agree for the Hot Core and for one component of the Compact Ridge.

why_this_method.value: Conventional rotation diagram with partition function including v_t up to 2

evidence.quote: Therefore, we calculated the partition function up to $v_{t} =$2 as discussed above.

limitations_admitted.value: Many lines blended; Hot Core v_t=2 T_rot not determinable

evidence.quote: It was not possible to determine the realistic rotational temperature of HCOOCH$_{3}$ in $v_{t} =$2 for the Hot Core.
